subject: Deletion sampling and retention matrix — SOC 2 evidence request
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@clearbank.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: audit_ops@clearbank.com
Date: 2026-10-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deletion sampling and retention matrix — SOC 2 evidence request

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the intro earlier. ClearBank is preparing our annual SOC 2 scope confirmation and we need a compact packet showing Redwood's retention/erasure controls for customer tenant data. Our audit team specifically asked for: 

- A current retention matrix mapping data categories (logs, generated outputs, KV cache, model context, backups) to TTLs and legal/contractual rationale.
- The sampling methodology used to verify deletion events (how you select tenants/keys, what logs are captured, and the cryptographic or checksum evidence you retain).
- Representative deletion logs/sample outputs (sanitized) for one tenant deletion cycle in the last 12 months.
- Confirmation of cross-region deletion behavior and whether any replication lag can leave copies outside the stated TTL window.

Can you provide a timeline for a small evidence bundle (PDF index + 2–3 sample logs) by Oct 22? If there are any required NDAs or redaction steps for logs, let me know.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to keep Redwood in scope for the audit.

Emma
Emma Clark
Senior Security Operations Manager
ClearBank

Subject: Re: Deletion sampling and retention matrix — SOC 2 evidence request

Thanks Mina — this looks promising. A couple of follow-ups from our audit team: 

- For "background object lifecycle GC" you mentioned, can you confirm whether objects in long-term blob tiers (cold storage) are physically deleted within your TTL window or only marked for deletion and eventually reclaimed by provider lifecycle jobs? We need to know if there are any windows where copies may persist beyond the TTL.
- For cached KV entries that power inference latency (in-memory+on-disk cache), please describe whether you have a persistent eviction record and whether evicted entries generate a deletion_event in the audit trail.
- Regarding sampling: please include the deterministic seed or approach used for reproducibility (so the auditor can confirm sampling was unbiased).

Finally, can you confirm the format of the index PDF we can expect and if you'll provide checksums (SHA256) for the sample logs? That helps us ingest the files into our evidence repository.

If we get the index and one sample by Oct 22, we'll do a quick internal review and come back with any redline requests.

Emma

On a separate note: would you be able to include a short paragraph confirming Redwood's policy on retention overrides (e.g., legal hold process) so we can mark it in our map?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clark <emma.clark@clearbank.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deletion sampling and retention matrix — SOC 2 evidence request

Emma — following up with concrete answers and artifacts. Summary below and attached sample log + evidence index.

1) Blob tiers and physical deletion
- For hot/warm blobs we perform immediate metadata tombstoning and asynchronous object GC. For cold/archival tiers (our provider-managed glacier-like tier) objects are marked as deleted and reclaimed according to provider retention windows. Our retention_matrix_v1.xlsx lists the tier-specific TTL and the maximum replication/reclamation window; by policy the maximum exposure past TTL is 72 hours for metadata and up to 7 days for deep archive reclamation in extreme cases. We include this as a note in the matrix.

2) Cached KV entries
- Cache eviction: we persist eviction events at the control plane level. An eviction generates a deletion_event record (control-plane audit log) that includes key hash, eviction timestamp, and reason (eviction/tenant-request/TTL). These are included in deletion-sample-log-2026-09.csv. In-memory evictions only are not persistent without the control-plane entry.

3) Sampling reproducibility
- Sampling was done with a deterministic seed (HMAC-SHA256 of date + team-key) and documented in sampling_plan_v1.pdf. We'll include the seed and the sample selection script (sanitized) so auditors can recompute the sample.

4) Checksums and index
- The evidence bundle will include SHA256 checksums for each file in the index (soc2-evidence-index.pdf). Attached: soc2-evidence-index.pdf and deletion-sample-log-2026-09.csv (sanitized).

5) Retention override / legal hold
- Legal hold process: holds are represented as a control-plane flag that prevents lifecycle rules from expiring objects. Holds require approval (legal or security) and are recorded in the audit log; we will include a one-paragraph excerpt from our legal-hold SOP in the index.

Attachments included in this message: soc2-evidence-index.pdf, deletion-sample-log-2026-09.csv. If you need any of the artifacts in a specific ISO/NIST mapping format, tell us and we will produce a mapping table.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
